name: distance_between_two_faces
why: The case that the API survey asked for by name: on a 40x40x10 plate, between the two large faces, the distance must be 10 mm. SOLIDWORKS gives it in METRES -- 0.01 -- and a wrong factor of a thousand would give 10 where the true value is 0.01: both read as plausible millimetres, and neither gives an error.
_why_the_deviation: the number arrives together with the TWO POINTS between which it was measured, and their distance is recomputed separately. If the value said zero and the points were four millimetres apart, the call would have failed and answered anyway. The deviation between the two calculations is an expectation in its own right: it is the only independent check we have on that number.

expect.tolerance_why: it is the thickness of the plate; SOLIDWORKS gives it in metres and the conversion is in the operation
the same number, redone from the two points
the two calculations must give the same number, not a similar one

expect.why: the answer also says where the conversion comes from
